name: Prompt Caching Planner
blurb: a prompt's parts ordered for provider prompt caching, with the cache breakpoints and the saving per call
intro: Lays a prompt out as parts from stable to volatile, places the cache breakpoints, replays a trace of calls against the provider's caching rules (Anthropic cache_control breakpoints, OpenAI automatic prefix caching, Gemini explicit context caching) and says which parts are read from cache, written or re-sent, and what that saves per call and per month. Rules and prices are a dated snapshot (2026-09): check them against the provider's documentation.

inputs.label: Prompt parts, in prompt order
inputs.help: Changes: how often the part's text differs between calls (per user = the same for one user's calls). Breakpoint after = a cache_control marker on the part's last block (Anthropic, at most 4; Gemini uses the last one as the explicit cache boundary; OpenAI ignores them and caches automatically).

inputs.label: Cache lifetime
inputs.help: Anthropic: 5m (write 1.25x input) or 1h (write 2x), refreshed by each read. OpenAI: 5m = in-memory retention (5-10 min idle), 24h = extended retention where the model offers it. Gemini: the explicit cache's TTL, billed as storage per hour.

inputs.label: Call trace (minute and user per line)
inputs.help: One call per line: the start minute and a user id. Calls of the same user share their per-user parts.

inputs.label: Calls per day (for the monthly figure)

examples.title: A support assistant with a timestamp above the retrieved manual (the prefix breaks every call)
The same prompt re-ordered stable to volatile, 1-hour TTL

usage: Give `parts` in prompt order as rows {name, tokens, changes: never|per day|per user|per call, bp: yes|no (a cache breakpoint after the part)}, the `model` (Claude, GPT-5 or Gemini ids from the options), the cache `ttl` (5m, 1h, 24h) and a `calls` trace (one 'minute user' per line). It replays the trace under that provider's caching rules and returns per-call hits, reads and writes, the cost per call with and without caching, the monthly saving at `calls_day`, warnings for a volatile part above stable ones, timestamp- or ID-like parts, prefixes under the model's minimum and misplaced breakpoints, a suggested stable-to-volatile order, the ordered layout and an Anthropic Messages JSON skeleton with cache_control placed. Rules and prices are dated (2026-09) and must be checked at the provider's docs.
sources: Anthropic docs 'Prompt caching' (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching): cache_control {type: ephemeral, ttl 5m|1h}, at most 4 breakpoints, prefix order tools -> system -> messages, minimum cacheable length per model (512 on Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Fable 5.1, 1024 on Sonnet 4.6, 4096 on Haiku 4.5), write 1.25x (5 min) or 2x (1 h) input, reads per model ($0.20 Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, $0.25 Fable 5.1, 0.1x otherwise), reads refresh the TTL - as cached by the Claude API reference on 2026-09-25

OpenAI 'Prompt caching' guide (platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching): automatic for prompts of 1024 tokens or more, hits in 128-token increments, no write fee, entries kept 5-10 minutes idle (extended 24 h retention on some models) - remembered at build time, not verified

Google 'Context caching' (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching): explicit caches with a TTL (default 1 h), minimum size per model, reads at the cached-token rate plus storage per million tokens per hour - numbers remembered at build time, not verified

Hit model: a breakpoint's cache key is the exact text of every part before it; a part's text changes as its 'changes' column says; the longest live breakpoint prefix is read, later breakpoints are written
